title: Direct image preserves constructible towers
statement:
Work in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix primes $p\ne\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; more generally the assertion holds for a separated finite-type $k$-morphism with all geometric fibres of dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Fix a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. On the derived categories of the coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], put
$$Rf_{!,\bullet}=R\bar f_{*,\bullet}\circ j_{!,\bullet}:D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))\longrightarrow D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(Y,\mathcal O_E)),$$
where $j_{!,\bullet}$ is levelwise extension by zero. With the levelwise identification of [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels], equivalently clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels], one has
$$(Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet)_n\simeq Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n.$$
If $C_\bullet\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], then $Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$. Here finite-level $\Dctf$ and Tor amplitude have the meaning of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. No normalization of the input tower is required.

proof.text: The section-normalized coordinates of lem-sp-tower-section-coordinates compare the sequence-site realization with ordinary finite-level evaluation. For any two recorded abelian presentations, their sections, restrictions and morphisms agree by the fields of sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, so their ordinary evaluation functors are equal by extensionality. Derive this ordinary comparison using mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso. Compose it with Fcomparison from det-sp-tower-shriek-levels and the derived equivalence counit to obtain the natural compact-support evaluation isomorphism, including its restriction to D+.

source.place: The single proof paragraph: finite-level preservation, followed by the uniform interval argument.

proof.text: The exact realization and exact open extension preserve every lower cohomological bound. The proper direct image is a total right derived functor, which is left t-exact on bounded-below objects: compare its bounded-below derived functor and use vanishing below the bound (CategoryTheory.Functor.isGE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj). The inverse exact realization preserves that bound too. For a constructible finite-Tor tower, use its given common cohomological interval from sk-def-sp-normalized-towers. Exact evaluation commutes with homology; strict systems detect zero levelwise and the presentation equivalence reflects zero. Hence the input tower is bounded below. The generic derived-category left-exactness argument is a proved source-library tool, not the constructibility assertion of that module.

proof.text: Apply det-sp-tower-bound-uniform with the common input Tor interval [v,w]. In the smooth case base change preserves the given relative dimension, and topologicalKrullDim_le_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension gives the geometric fibre bound. In the general case specialize the given bound to algebraic closures of residue fields. The actual coefficient ring R_n is killed by ell^(n+1), since ell^(n+1) belongs to the defining ideal (ell)^(n+1); it is finite by the supplied Base. Thus clause (1) of the uniform theorem proves finite-level constructibility for the actual finite compact-support image. Compare its open-extension left adjoint with the intrinsic one using the normalized pullback comparison def-trf-finite-pullback-coordinate-comparison and uniqueness of left adjoints; derive and compose with the fixed proper direct image. Transfer finite constructibility to the tower output using the level comparison. Constructibility is invariant under isomorphism via lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility.

source.place: The single proof paragraph: finite-level preservation, followed by the uniform interval argument.

proof.text: Clause (2) of det-sp-tower-bound-uniform already gives both the common output Tor interval [v,w+2d] and vanishing of cohomology outside it. Transfer the input hypotheses across the realization-level comparison, apply that clause to the realized input tower, and transfer the conclusion across the inverse realization counit and its level comparison. Tor amplitude is invariant under isomorphism directly from its definition, by composing the representative isomorphism. Combine these uniform bounds with finite-level constructibility from step 3 to construct exactly spConstructibleTorTowers on the output. No normalization hypothesis is used.
